Where design students find their people.

CoLab is a skill-first platform where students and professionals discover collaborators, build project teams, and bring great ideas to life.

Role  Product & Brand Design Type  Mobile app concept Scope  Research → Brand → UI Tools  Figma
SCROLL ↓
THE GIST

Talent isn’t scarce. Finding it is.

Design students sit beside hundreds of talented peers, yet the right collaborator stays invisible — buried in WhatsApp groups, scattered portfolios and the same three friends. CoLab makes skills visible and teams easy to build, so great ideas reach the right people.

THE PROBLEM
Skills are invisible; collaboration is fragmented.
THE INSIGHT
It’s friction, not a lack of talent.
THE USERS
Design students & early professionals.
THE OUTCOME
A skill-first collaboration app + brand.
The Problem Space

Students and professionals consistently struggle to build the right teams — not because talent is scarce, but because skills are invisible.

Finding skilled peers is hard

There’s no way to search people by the exact skill a project needs.

Collaboration is scattered

Work is spread across WhatsApp, Instagram, Drive and Notion.

Contributions get lost

Individual work isn’t credited, so portfolios don’t grow.

Opportunities stay in circles

Projects never leave an existing, immediate social circle.

Great work can’t travel

Strong work struggles to reach the right collaborators.

Limited collaboration, limited learning

Fewer teams means fewer chances to grow and be seen.

Your immediate social circle
Skills like motion, branding, photography and set design sit just outside reach — real, but unsearchable.

SWOT

Strengths

  • Only platform built for design students
  • Skill-based matching, not generic
  • Portfolio auto-builds on project end
  • Academic context (deadlines, years)
  • Peer-rated collaboration history

Weaknesses

  • Cold-start problem — no users at launch
  • Requires active profile maintenance
  • Dependent on institution buy-in

Opportunities

  • Rapid growth in design education in India
  • No direct competitor in this niche
  • EdTech growing at 13–28% CAGR
  • Expand to engineering & MBA
  • Freelancing marketplace in Phase 3

Threats

  • LinkedIn adding student features
  • Discord/Slack as informal alternatives
  • Low willingness to pay among students
  • Institutions building internal tools
SO  Skill-based differentiation WO  Institutional partnerships ST  Early community building WT  Frictionless onboarding
Sources: British Council — The Future of Design Education in India · India Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF).

Empathy map — Amit Kumar

What Amit thinks, feels, says and does when trying to find collaborators.

Thinks

  • “Will anyone even respond to my request?”
  • “I need a motion designer — no idea who has that skill.”
  • “I always end up with the same 3 friends.”
  • “Is this even for students or just pros?”

Feels

  • Frustrated — the skills he needs are invisible
  • Anxious — the deadline is 3 weeks away, no team
  • Excited when he finds a skilled peer by chance
  • Undervalued when his work isn’t attributed

Says

  • “I couldn’t find anyone for motion in my batch.”
  • “Why isn’t there a LinkedIn but for students?”
  • “I always work with the same people — I trust them.”
  • “WhatsApp groups get chaotic fast for project work.”

Does

  • Posts in class WhatsApp broadcasts seeking teammates
  • Scrolls Behance & Instagram for peer portfolios
  • Settles for a smaller scope to fit the team he has
  • Tracks tasks alone in Notion when the team falls through

The problem isn’t a lack of talent. It’s the friction in finding, trusting and collaborating.
The Solution

Eight moves that turn invisible skills into real teams — each one answering a frustration the research surfaced.

01

Skill-tagged profiles & search

Every student is searchable by the exact skill — motion, 3D, branding, research.

Solves: skills are invisible
02

Post a project, get applications

Describe the project and role; interested peers apply instead of you cold-DMing.

Solves: opportunities stay in circles
03

Skill-based top matches

Ranked collaborator suggestions based on the skill gaps your project has.

Solves: hard to find the right people
04

Build a squad + real-time chat

Invite, confirm roles and talk — all in one place, not five apps.

Solves: collaboration is scattered
05

Lightweight workspace

Projects, to-dos, activity and workspace health keep a team moving.

Solves: unequal workloads, silence
06

Peer ratings & history

Collaboration reviews build trust before you ever reach out.

Solves: unreliable teammates
07

Portfolio auto-build

Finished projects roll into a portfolio, with contributions credited.

Solves: contributions get lost
08

Academic context

Deadlines, year and discipline make matches relevant to campus life.

Solves: built for students

Brand & Design System

A visual identity built on three ideas — structure, creativity and growth — expressed through one confident wordmark.

The logo

  • CO grabs attention first.
  • The arrow shows direction — upward momentum.
  • Lab completes the meaning: a place to make.

Structure — collaboration & clarity · Creativity — ideas & human connection · Growth — forward momentum.

Colour

#BAEB05
Energy, innovation, growth
#F7F2E8
Clean, open, clear
#0B0B0B
Professional, focused

Type

BEBAS NEUE
Headings & CTAs — bold, impactful, confident.
HeadingBebas Neue
Sub-headingHelvetica Neue (Medium)
ParagraphHelvetica Neue (Regular)
CTA / buttonsBebas Neue

Why it works

Bebas Neue is modern and easy to notice. Helvetica Neue keeps everything clean and readable. The lime-led palette balances trust with innovation — creative, but credible.

The result reads as a tool students actually want to open: playful, high-contrast and unmistakably CoLab.

Logo iterations

From “Collaborative / Teams / Momentum / Visibility / Create” toward a single mark with an upward arrow.

Reflection & Next Steps

What the project taught me, and where CoLab goes from here.

Design the friction, not the featureResearch kept pointing back to one thing — discovery. Leading with skill-search, not another feed, is what makes CoLab different.
Serve two users, one needA 2nd-year student and a 4.5-year professional want the same thing: the right people, less friction. The brand had to feel credible to both.
Brand is part of the UXA bold, confident identity is what gets students to open a “boring” category — collaboration — in the first place.
Plan for the cold startThe biggest risk is an empty app at launch, so the roadmap leans on institutional partnerships and early community building.

Roadmap

PHASE 01

Prove it on campus

  • Launch with one design school
  • Skill search, projects & squads
  • Seed early community
PHASE 02

Grow the network

  • Institutional partnerships
  • Expand to engineering & MBA
  • Peer ratings at scale
PHASE 03

Open the marketplace

  • Student freelancing marketplace
  • Paid briefs & commissions
  • Portfolio → opportunity loop
